lines.text: תנך 1140 תער
* II. תְּנַן Chald. i. q. ܬܢ̇ܢ, to smoke;
whence Eth. ተን, ἀτμίς, vapour; Chald.
תְּנָנָא, Syr. ܬܶܢܳܢܳܐ, ܬܽܘܢܳܢܳܐ, Sam. ࠕࠍࠍࠀ,
smoke; Nasor. חאנא furnace.
Deriv. Chald. אַתּוּן, comp. תַּנּוּר.
תִּנְשֶׁמֶת f. (r. נָשַׁם to respire) 1. Lev.
11, 30, an unclean animal, classed with
other species of lizards; according to
Bochart (Hieroz. T. I. p. 1083) the cha-
melion, so called as living upon air ac-
cording to the opinion of the ancients,
Plin. H. N. 8. 33. Hasselquist Reise
p. 350. Sept. and Vulg. talpa, mole.
Saad. lizard.
2. Lev. 11, 18. Deut. 14, 16, an unclean
aquatic bird, prob. the pelican, pelecanus
onocrotalus, so called from its pouch,
which it can extend by inflation, see
Oedm. Verm. Samml. III. 50.—Sept.
πορφυρίων, i. e. the crested purple heron,
ardea purpurea Linn. Vulg. cygnus,
swan.
* תָּעַב in Kal not used; comp. תָּאַב
II. This root is very rarely found in
the other Semitic dialects in its usual
Hebrew signification. The primary
idea seems to be to thrust forth or away,
to drive away; and hence to reject, to
abhor, to abominate.
Piel תִּעֵב, fut. יְתַעֵב 1. to abominate,
to abhor, Deut. 7, 26. 23, 8. Am. 5, 10.
2. Causat. to cause to abhor, to fill
one with abhorrence. Is. 49, 7 מְתָעֵב גּוֹי
who causeth abhorrence to the people,
who is an abomination to the people.
3. Causat. to make abominable, to
cause to be abhorred, Job 9, 31. Ez. 16,
25. See Hiph.
Hiph. to make abominable, shameful.
Ps. 14, 1 הִתְעִיבוּ עֲלִילָה they make abom-
inable their doings, i. e. they do abom-
inable deeds, act abominably; comp. Ps.
53, 2. So with עֲלִילָה implied id. 1 K.
Niph. pass. to be an abomination, ab-
horred, detestable, 1 Chr. 21, 6. Part.
נִתְעָב abominable Job 15, 16; despised,
worthless, Is. 14, 19.
Deriv. תּוֹעֵבָה.
* תָּעָה fut. יִתְעֶה, apoc. יֵתַע, pr. ‘to
be thrust hither and thither,’ comp.
תָּעַע; kindr. is תָּעַב q. v. Then, like r.
טָעָה, to wander, to err, to go astray
Chald. תְּעָא id. but oftener טְעָא; Syr.
ܛܥܳܐ, Arab. طغا and طغى id. Spoken
of persons Is. 35, 8. 47, 15; of beasts
כְּשֶׂה אֹבֵד I have gone astray like a lost
sheep; also of birds Job 38, 41; with בְּ
With acc. of place, to wander through
or over, trop. of the branches of a vine
shooting luxuriantly over the desert, Is.
16, 9 [8]. Spec. a) Of drunken per-
sons, who go reeling about; Is. 28, 7
תָּעוּ מִן־הַשֵּׁכָר they go astray (reel) from
strong drink; and hence trop. of the
mind, Is. 21, 4 תָּעָה לְבָבִי my heart reel-
eth, is seized with giddiness. b) Trop.
of the mind as erring from the paths of
virtue and piety, Ps. 58, 4. Ez. 48, 11;
comp. תֹּעֵי לֵבָב Ps. 95, 10, תֹּעֵי רוּחַ Is. 29,
24. With מִן, e. g. from God’s precepts
Ps. 119, 110, comp. Prov. 21, 16; with
מֵעַל יְהֹוָה Ez. 44, 10. 15; with מֵאַחֲרֵי
יְהֹוָה from following God, from his wor-
ship, Ez. 14, 11. Comp. Chald. טְעָא
spec. ‘ to be given to idolatry,’ Syr. to
be a heretic. c) Of those who miss
their aim and fail in their efforts; Prov.
14, 22 הֲלוֹא יִתְעוּ חֹרְשֵׁי רָע do they not
err (from their mark) who devise evil?
Others, do they not perish.
Niph. to wander, pr. to be made to
wander, to stagger about, Is. 19, 14.
Metaph. to be deceived, to err, in a mor-
al sense, Job 15, 31.
Hiph. fut. apoc. יֶ֫תַע 1. to cause to
wander Job 12, 24. Is. 19, 13. 14. Gen.
drunken man Job 12, 25. Is. 30, 28 רֶסֶן
מַתְעֶה a bridle causing to err. Metaph.
to cause to wander or err from the paths
of virtue and piety, e. g. a nation into
impiety, ungodliness, Is. 3, 12. 9, 15.
into idolatry, 2 K. 21, 9. 2 Chr. 33, 9;
with מִן Is. 63, 17.
2. Intrans. to err, pr. to let oneself
wander, Jer. 42, 20 Keri. Prov. 10, 17.
Deriv. תּוֹעָה, and
תֹּעוּ (error) Tou, pr. n. of a king of
Hamath or Epiphania, 1 Chr. 18, 9. 10;
written תֹּעִי Toi 2 Sam. 8, 9. 10.
תְּעוּדָה f. (r. עוּד Hiph.) a divine pre-
cept; hence an oracle Is. 8, 16; law,

line_status.note: The word after "i. q." is printed in Syriac script (same letterforms as the Syr. items on line 3: a taw at the right, two nuns with a descending final), with a single point above the nun — not Arabic تَنَّ. Reading B's Syriac is correct; the Hebrew תְּנַן and "to smoke ;" are the same in both.

The Ethiopic word is printed as a cross-shaped ተ (tä) followed by a 7-shaped ን (nə) — ተን "tan", smoke — not ጢስ (which would show a looped ጠ-form); a thin space is also printed before the semicolon after "vapour", matching Reading B.

In the second Syriac word the waw (the small "o") is printed immediately after the taw (ܬܘܢܢܐ), not after the first nun as in B; and Syriac vowel points are clearly printed (dots/circles above the nuns and marks at the taw), which B omits.

The rightmost (first) letter of the Hebrew word is printed as ח: flat top bar with two plain legs and no left foot. Compare the tav in תְּנַן on line 1, which clearly shows the foot on the left leg; this glyph lacks it. So the printed word is חאנא, not תאנא. Remaining letters אנא and the Latin text agree in both readings.
The future form's first (rightmost) letter is a short yod with sheva, not a tav; the printed form is יְתַעֵב (3 m. sg.), so Reading B is correct.

Printed left-to-right order after "Comp." is הִשְׁחִית first (immediately following "Comp."), then a comma, then הֵרַע at the line's end; Reading A reverses the two items. All points agree in both readings and match the print (הִשְׁחִית with shin dot, sheva, two hiriqs and plene yod; הֵרַע with tsere and patah).
Initial letter is a rounded closed-bowl teth (ט) with qamets, no dagesh; not tav. Consistent with Arabic cognate طغا (ṭ) and Chaldee טְעָא on the following lines.

The only difference is the point order inside the tetragrammaton. In the print the holem dot sits above the he (at the he/vav junction), not above the vav, so the sequence is he+holem, vav+qamets (יְהֹוָה) as in B, not vav+holem+qamets (יְהוָֹה) as in A. Everything else (מֵעַל, "Ez. 44, 10. 15; with", מֵאַחֲרֵי with hataf-patah under het and tsere under resh) is identical in both readings and matches the print.

The holem dot is printed over the he (הֹ), not over the vav; the vav carries only qamets (וָ). So the sequence is he+holem, vav+qamets, as in Reading B. Reading A places holem on the vav after the qamets, which does not match the print.

The printed quotation marks are typographic single quotes (inverted-comma ‘ opening, raised-comma ’ closing), not straight ASCII apostrophes; otherwise the two readings are identical and match the print.
Printed form is three letters (yod-tav-ayin), no vav prefix as in B; but the yod has segol below and a stress accent above, not patach as in A. No dagesh visible.
The vowel under ע is a qamets (bar with descending tick), not tsere; compare the clearly dotted tsere under ע in the next line's תֹּעוּ. Dagesh in ת and holem on ו as both readings have.
